newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe agrees with year loss estimates.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe agrees with year loss estimates.

text.p: CompuServe Corp Chief Financial Officer Lawrence Gyenes said Friday the company is comfortable with analysts' estimates that it will post a loss of $0.65-$0.78 a share for the fiscal year ending April 30, excluding previously reported one-time writeoffs.
CompuServe earned $0.66 a share in the previous year.
Chairman and acting Chief Executive Officer Frank Salizzoni said he could not predict when the online provider might return to profitability but said CompuServe is "moving in the right direction."
"We still have a ways to go, but hopefully, in the not-too-distant future, we'll get back to profitability," he said.
Gyenes and Salizzoni spoke to reporters after the annual meeting at CompuServe's headquarters.
Asked about the range of analysts' estimates, compiled by First Call, Gyenes said, "We're comfortable with that range... We'll be within shouting distance of those figures."
CompuServe's corporate services provider, Network Services, has done well in the current fiscal year, but its consumer online service has struggled.
For the first three quarters of the year, the company reported a loss of $1.10 a share, but it narrowed its loss in the third quarter from the second.
The third quarter also included the first positive operational cash flow in five quarters.
Tax preparer H&R Block Inc owns 80 percent of CompuServe.
